title: Local-business status beside a larger or out-of-State owner
question: Which firms shown with local-business status belong to an owner-group that includes a large or out-of-area firm?
finding: Of 1,111 names shown with local-business status in the City’s contract file, 135 are tied to another name and 4 of those ties are to a firm without that status that is large or registered only outside California: 1 on record evidence (tiers 1 to 4) and 3 on a shared address only. The largest: Ransome Company beside Silverado Contractors Inc. (2: same licensed person). 739 names carry both statuses in different contracts. The State’s certified disadvantaged-business directory could not be downloaded, so it was not tested.
how: Local-business status is the "LBE" flag the Controller’s contract file prints beside each prime contractor, subcontractor and joint-venture member. Each flagged name is looked up in the owner-groups (tiers 1 to 4) and address leads (tier 5). A tie is listed when the other name does not carry the flag and either was paid at least $5 million and five times as much as the flagged firm since fiscal 2019, or is registered in the business registry only at addresses outside California.
limits: The size and ownership limits for local-business certification are not in any file on disk and should be checked before reading a row as a problem; a certified firm may share an office with, or be a joint-venture partner of, a large firm, and most tier 5 rows are exactly that. The flag is as recorded on each contract and may predate or postdate a change of ownership. The City’s certified-firm directory with owners, and the State directory of disadvantaged businesses (behind a CAPTCHA), are not on disk.
